title: Call parameter validation explainability and interactive repair advisor
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Problem: engineers and integrators repeatedly hit opaque JSON validation failures when calling tools/function endpoints. Current failures are terse tokens/errors with little context, forcing trial-and-error and support involvement. This ticket proposes an end-to-end feature: a validation explainability layer that turns raw schema errors into actionable, ranked repair suggestions plus a small compatibility adaptor surface for older SDKs. The goal is to reduce time-to-fix for integration bugs and reduce support tickets by surfacing human-friendly diagnostics, repair recipes (single-line fixes or coercion toggles), and telemetry hooks for confidence scoring. The feature covers author-time (SDK linting/CLI), runtime (error envelopes and soft-enforcement modes), and streaming scenarios (incremental validation checkpoints for partial outputs).
acceptance_criteria: IDL: define an invocation JSON-IDL that supports typed fields, optional/required annotations, deprecation markers, and delta-version metadata; published in the runtime-schema-ux Confluence page

Explainability: runtime returns an error envelope with a machine error code, short human message, failed-field path(s), example payload snippet, and at least two ranked repair suggestions (coercion, defaulting, field rename), formatted for both SDK and Console
Soft enforcement: implement a runtime flag (soft_validation=true) that emits warnings (non-2xx) in telemetry but still returns a best-effort result when safe; documented and guarded by rate limits
Compatibility adapter: build a lightweight SDK adapter for Python and Node that translates legacy flat-arg payloads into the new IDL with best-effort heuristics and emits deprecation warnings
Streaming validation: add checkpointed validators that validate completed segments of streaming structured output and include checkpoint errors in the streaming event envelope
Observability: add telemetry signals (validation_error_count, top_5_failing_paths, repair_suggestion_accept_rate) to Console dashboards and link to a new runtime-2026.04 release dashboard
Tests: unit tests for validator, integration tests exercising soft enforcement and compatibility adapter, and an end-to-end smoke test with example tool definitions
steps: Draft JSON-IDL spec: shape, optional/required, deprecation, examples, and migration rules; get PM + Design signoff
Implement validator library (Go) used by runtime with clear error code enums and repair hint builder
Extend runtime error envelope to include explainability fields and telemetry hooks
Add SDK adapters for Python/Node; wire emitters for human-friendly messages and quick-fix snippets
Add Console change: display structured validation detail in the request inspector and surface suggested fixes in the request log
Write integration and streaming checkpoint tests; run load-test to validate soft-enforcement performance impact
Publish docs and migration guide; announce in #dev-platform and update Quickstart templates
notes: Repair suggestions are finite heuristic recipes, not guaranteed transforms. Each suggestion must include confidence level (high|medium|low) and an example payload after applying the suggestion
We should avoid automatic server-side mutation of user payloads unless customer opts into an explicit flag (auto_repair=true) and accepts legal/audit implications
Schema delta markers: include a small version tag in every tool manifest to allow runtime to pick compatible coercion rules
For streaming outputs, validators will run on newline- or record-delimited chunks; we will not buffer arbitrarily long streams for validation
Telemetry: sample repair suggestions acceptance at 1% by default to avoid large cardinality; increase sampling if customers opt-in
